title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Operating Procedures, and Top Support Issues
author: Maya Patel
body:
Purpose

This page documents the canonical Developer Experience (DevEx) artifacts and operating procedures for SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site publishing, and the canonical fixes for our top support issues. It is intended for SDK authors, technical writers, solutions engineers, and on-call support engineers.

Scope

- SDK Guides: full-reference guides and migration notes for official Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go).
- Quickstarts & Templates: short, runnable quickstarts and repo templates for common integration patterns.
- API Examples: copy-paste REST and SDK examples used in docs and onboarding flows.
- Docs Site Operating Procedures: publishing workflow, review checklist, and CI preview process.
- Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes: triage playbook and canned responses for the most frequent developer-facing tickets.

Owners and Roles

- Primary owner: Developer Experience (DevEx) — owner_team: engineering.
- Document owner (single point of contact): Maya Patel (DevEx).
- Reviewers: assigned from SDK, product, and support (see metadata).
- Escalation: if an issue requires infra or runtime changes, escalate to Eng-Platform oncall and open a ticket with PROD-RUNTIME label.

Standards & Templates

All DevEx pages must follow these standards:

- Tone: concise, example-driven, prescriptive. Use complete sentences and clear headings.
- Page structure: short intro, prerequisites, step-by-step quickstart, copyable code snippets, troubleshooting section, and links to related pages.
- Verify examples: all CLI and SDK examples must be runnable in CI (docs-ci) and pass smoke tests.
- Versioning: include a top-level "Last tested with" line with SDK and API versions.

SDK Guide Template (use for full reference docs)

Recommended headings for a full SDK guide:

1) Title and short description
2) Supported platforms and languages
3) Installation and compatibility
   - Package name and pinned versions
   - Example: pip install redwood-sdk==1.8.2
4) Authentication and configuration
   - Environment variables, config file, common pitfalls
5) Core concepts and usage patterns
   - Rate limiting, batching, streaming, retries
6) Code examples (minimal + advanced)
7) Error handling and best practices
8) Migration notes (if replacing older SDKs or breaking changes)
9) Troubleshooting and FAQs
10) Changelog and "Last tested with" metadata

Quickstart Template (single-file, ~5-10 minute run)

- Purpose: show a minimal end-to-end flow (auth -> call -> handle response).
- Estimated time to complete: 5 minutes.
- Prerequisites: Redwood account, API key, Python 3.10+ or Node 18+.
- Steps:
  1. Install the SDK (one-liner).
  2. Export API key or configure via CLI.
  3. Run a single example that prints a response.
  4. Small troubleshooting tips for common local issues.

Example Quickstart (Python)

- File: quickstart.py
- Minimal content:

```python
import os
from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1-3b", input="Write a friendly two-line product tagline for Redwood Inference.")
print(resp.text)
```

Shell install and run:

```bash
python -m pip install redwood-sdk==1.8.2
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxxxxxxx
python quickstart.py
```

API Examples (canonical snippets)

Provide two canonical pathways: REST/cURL and Python/TypeScript SDKs. Keep examples small and opinionated.

1) REST / cURL (HTTP)

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-3b","input":"Translate to French: What a lovely day"}'
```

2) Python SDK (recommended pattern)

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])
result = client.generate(model="redwood-1-3b", input="Summarize: The quarterly roadmap focuses on infra and reliability improvements.")
print(result.text)
```

3) TypeScript SDK (Node)

```ts
import { Redwood } from "@redwood/inference"
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const resp = await client.generate({ model: "redwood-1-3b", input: "List three ways to reduce inference cost." })
console.log(resp.text)
```

Docs Site Operating Procedures (publishing workflow)

1) Authoring
- Create/update Markdown or Confluence page in the devex repo.
- Add owner and reviewers in the front matter or page header.
- Include "Last tested with" metadata (SDK + API version).

2) CI / Preview
- Push branch to docs repo. Docs CI (docs-ci) runs linting, link-checker, and smoke tests that execute minimal examples in containers.
- A preview site is generated and posted as a netlify/preview link in the PR within ~10 minutes.

3) Review and Approve
- Reviewer checklist (see below) must be completed in PR.
- At least one DevEx reviewer + one SDK owner must approve for API or code changes.

4) Merge and Publish
- Merge triggers full build and deploy to the staging site. After a 2-hour monitoring window, merge to main publishes to production docs site.
- For critical fixes (security/credentials), use the "hotfix" pipeline: mark PR with label hotfix/docs; on merge, docs team will notify #docs-alerts and perform an expedited production deploy.

Reviewer Checklist (must be completed before merge)

- [ ] Examples run locally and in docs-ci (pass smoke tests).
- [ ] Code snippets are minimal and follow SDK best practices (no deprecated calls).
- [ ] All external links resolve and are HTTPS.
- [ ] Schematic diagrams and architecture references updated if relevant.
- [ ] Accessibility: headings, alt text for images, keyboard navigation verified.
- [ ] API surface changes are aligned with SDK owners and product.

Docs Metrics & SLOs

- Docs CI pass rate: maintain >= 98% on published branches.
- Example smoke tests: 100% green for published quickstarts.
- Hotfix SLA: security-sensitive docs updated and published within 24 hours of detection.

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (triage playbook)

The items below are the most common developer-facing issues and our canonical responses/fixes. Support should follow the triage steps and use the canned replies where appropriate.

Issue: 401 / Authentication errors
- Symptom: 401 Unauthorized, "Invalid API Key".
- Canonical fixes:
  - Verify environment variable name (REDWOOD_API_KEY) and no accidental whitespace.
  - Confirm key scope and expiration in the console.
  - If using private deployment, ensure local config points to the correct endpoint and KMS is reachable.
- Canned response: "Please verify your API key is set as REDWOOD_API_KEY and that the key is active in the Redwood Console. If you rotated keys recently, make sure the running process picked up the new key."

Issue: 429 / Rate limit exceeded
- Symptom: 429 responses or "rate limit" errors.
- Canonical fixes:
  - Recommend client-side exponential backoff and jitter (base=500ms, factor=2, max=8s).
  - Suggest batching small requests where possible and increasing concurrency limits for Dedicated customers via support ticket.
- Sample retry header check: X-RateLimit-Remaining / X-RateLimit-Reset

Issue: 422 / Model or input validation errors
- Symptom: 422 Unprocessable Entity, model not found, or invalid param.
- Canonical fixes:
  - Confirm correct model id and that the model is available in the customer's region/tier.
  - Check payload schema: fields required by the API (model, input, max_tokens, temperature).

Issue: Streaming timeouts or truncated streams
- Symptom: client receives partial stream or connection closed early.
- Canonical fixes:
  - Suggest switching to the chunked/streaming SDK example in our docs and enabling keepalive headers.
  - Check proxy/load balancer timeouts; recommend timeout >= 120s for long generation sessions.

Issue: Embedding dimension mismatch
- Symptom: downstream indexer complains about vector length.
- Canonical fixes:
  - Validate the model used for embeddings and the expected vector dimension (document in SDK guide).
  - If migrating models, add a compatibility note and an automatic reindex job in the migration playbook.

Issue: High token cost complaints
- Symptom: customer reports unexpectedly high usage costs.
- Canonical fixes:
  - Review tokenization examples and demonstrate how to control max_tokens and top_p/temperature to reduce usage.
  - Recommend caching strategies (prefix caching, candidate reranking) and model size changes for cost-sensitive routes.

Canonical support templates (examples)

- Authentication 401 reply:
  "Thanks — the 401 indicates a problem with auth. Please confirm that you have exported your key as REDWOOD_API_KEY and that the key is active in the Console. If you still see 401 after confirming, reply with the request-id header from one failed request (X-Request-Id) so we can trace it."

- Rate limit guidance reply:
  "We see 429s. Please implement exponential backoff with jitter and consider batching. If you need sustained higher throughput, open a support request with expected QPS and payload size and we can evaluate a Dedicated capacity increase."

Troubleshooting Playbook (triage steps for support)

1) Collect logs and minimal repro (curl + headers).
2) Reproduce in a sandbox environment (docs-ci environment preferred).
3) Check console for key status, model availability, and rate-limiter metrics.
4) If the problem is client-side, provide a quick code diff and a unit test that reproduces the issue.
4) Escalate to Eng-Platform or Eng-Serving-Runtime if the request-id maps to an internal error (5xx) or capacity/latency degradation.

CI and Smoke Testing for Examples

- All quickstarts must include a smoke test (3–4 assertions) that runs in docs-ci. Examples that create resources must use ephemeral test projects.
- Failure modes: flaky examples should be quarantined and converted into integration tests that run less frequently (nightly).

Change Log and Maintenance Cadence

- Quarterly doc review: product + devex owners must review all quickstarts and SDK guides each quarter or whenever major API changes occur.
- Deprecation policy: mark deprecated examples with a banner and a migration guide; remove after 6 months of dual-run support.

Related resources

- Developer Experience docs site (how-to and operating procedures).
- SDK repositories: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk (link in repo index).
- Support runbook and escalation matrix (see eng-sre runbooks).

Appendix: Example doc front-matter (YAML)

```yaml
title: "Quickstart: Text Generation (Python)"
owner: "maya.patel@redwood.ai"
last_tested_with: "redwood-sdk==1.8.2, api=v1"
labels: ["quickstart","python","generation"]
```

If you have questions or proposed changes to this playbook, open a PR in the docs repo and tag @maya-patel and the DevEx Slack channel (#devex).
